title: Paperclip and the Gehlen network as a homecoming; Nazi Germany as a field laboratory

tellings.quote: that in a lot of ways both paperclip and the absorption of the Galen network were a homecoming. It's almost as if Nazi Germany was set up as a field laboratory to do some highly unethical things.

plain: After the Second World War, the US brought German scientists to America in a programme called Paperclip, and took over a German spy network run by an intelligence officer named Reinhard Gehlen. A researcher named Jason Jorjani tells podcast host Jesse Michels that both were really a "homecoming", and that it is almost as if Nazi Germany had been set up as a field laboratory to do highly unethical things. If true, it would mean the Nazi research was tied to American interests from the start.
